title: CTS Practical Theology — Unit 8: Christian Community & Accountability

blocks.en: 🌱 Practical Theology — Unit 8: Christian Community & Accountability
blocks.es_reference: 🌱 Teología Práctica — Unidad 8: La Comunidad Cristiana y la Rendición de Cuentas

blocks.en: Professors: Dr. Wayne Cook & Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesores: Dr. Wayne Cook y Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.es_reference: Introducción

blocks.en: No one was meant to follow Christ alone. The God who saves us does not save us into isolation; He saves us into a body and into a family. The disciplines we have studied so far — walking with God, devotion, prayer, the Word, self-discipline — are deeply personal, but they were never meant to be private. From the beginning God said, "It is not good that man should be alone" (Genesis 2:18, NKJV) — spoken first of marriage, but expressing a truth that runs through the whole of human life: we were not made for isolation. The same is true in the life of the Spirit. We are saved one by one, but we are saved into one another. This unit takes up two gifts our individualistic age has nearly forgotten: Christian community and loving accountability.
blocks.es_reference: Nadie fue hecho para seguir a Cristo en soledad. El Dios que nos salva no nos salva al aislamiento; nos salva a un cuerpo y a una familia. Las disciplinas que hemos estudiado — andar con Dios, la devoción, la oración, la Palabra, el dominio propio — son profundamente personales, pero nunca fueron pensadas para ser privadas. Desde el principio Dios dijo: "No es bueno que el hombre esté solo" (Génesis 2:18, RVG) — dicho primero acerca del matrimonio, pero expresando una verdad que recorre toda la vida humana: no fuimos hechos para el aislamiento. Lo mismo es cierto en la vida del Espíritu. Somos salvados uno por uno, pero somos salvados los unos para los otros. Esta unidad trata dos dones que nuestra época individualista casi ha olvidado: la comunidad cristiana y la rendición de cuentas amorosa.

blocks.en: I. We Belong to One Another
blocks.es_reference: I. Pertenecemos los Unos a los Otros

blocks.en: When a person trusts Christ, he is joined not only to the Lord but to all who belong to the Lord. Paul says it plainly: "Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually" (1 Corinthians 12:27, NKJV). A hand cannot say to the eye, "I have no need of you." Each member is necessary, and each belongs to the rest: "so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another" (Romans 12:5, NKJV). To be a Christian and to despise the people of God is a contradiction. We do not attend the body; we are the body.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando una persona confía en Cristo, queda unida no solo al Señor, sino a todos los que son del Señor. Pablo lo dice con claridad: "Vosotros, pues, sois el cuerpo de Cristo, y miembros en particular" (1 Corintios 12:27, RVG). La mano no puede decir al ojo: "No te necesito." Cada miembro es necesario, y cada uno pertenece a los demás: "así nosotros, siendo muchos, somos un cuerpo en Cristo, y todos miembros los unos de los otros" (Romanos 12:5, RVG). Ser cristiano y despreciar al pueblo de Dios es una contradicción. No asistimos al cuerpo; somos el cuerpo.

blocks.en: II. Do Not Forsake the Assembly
blocks.es_reference: II. No Dejéis de Congregaros

blocks.en: Because we belong to one another, Scripture commands us not to drift away from the gathered church. "And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching" (Hebrews 10:24–25, NKJV). The first church gave itself to this without reserve: "And they continued steadfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers" (Acts 2:42, NKJV). The local church is not optional equipment for the strong Christian; it is the ordinary place where God grows His people.
blocks.es_reference: Porque pertenecemos los unos a los otros, la Escritura nos manda no apartarnos de la iglesia reunida. "Y considerémonos unos a otros para provocarnos al amor y a las buenas obras; no dejando de congregarnos, como algunos tienen por costumbre, sino exhortándonos; y tanto más, cuanto veis que aquel día se acerca" (Hebreos 10:24–25, RVG). La primera iglesia se entregó a esto sin reservas: "Y perseveraban en la doctrina de los apóstoles, y en la comunión, y en el partimiento del pan, y en las oraciones" (Hechos 2:42, RVG). La iglesia local no es un accesorio opcional para el cristiano fuerte; es el lugar ordinario donde Dios hace crecer a su pueblo.

blocks.en: III. The "One Anothers"
blocks.es_reference: III. Los "Unos a Otros"

blocks.en: The New Testament is full of commands that cannot be obeyed alone. We are to love one another, serve one another, forgive one another, encourage one another, and bear with one another. Our Lord made love the badge of His followers: "A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you... By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another" (John 13:34–35, NKJV). Every "one another" assumes that we are close enough to one another to obey it.
blocks.es_reference: El Nuevo Testamento está lleno de mandamientos que no se pueden obedecer a solas. Debemos amarnos unos a otros, servirnos, perdonarnos, exhortarnos y sobrellevarnos. Nuestro Señor hizo del amor la señal de los suyos: "Un mandamiento nuevo os doy: Que os améis unos a otros; como yo os he amado... En esto conocerán todos que sois mis discípulos, si tuviereis amor los unos con los otros" (Juan 13:34–35, RVG). Cada "unos a otros" supone que estamos lo bastante cerca unos de otros como para obedecerlo.

blocks.en: IV. Watching Over One Another in Love — Accountability
blocks.es_reference: IV. Velar los Unos por los Otros en Amor — la Rendición de Cuentas

blocks.en: Accountability simply means that believers lovingly watch over one another's walk with God — encouraging, praying, and gently correcting. Centuries ago John Wesley gathered believers into small "class meetings" where they regularly asked one another a simple question: how is it with your soul? We keep our own convictions about the details, but the idea is sound and biblical: a few trusted believers who know us and will ask the honest questions. When someone stumbles, the command is gentle: "Brethren, if a man is overtaken in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness... Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ" (Galatians 6:1–2, NKJV). The Word tells us to be open with one another: "Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed" (James 5:16, NKJV). And it tells us why we need each other: "As iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the countenance of his friend" (Proverbs 27:17, NKJV). "Two are better than one... And a threefold cord is not quickly broken" (Ecclesiastes 4:9, 12, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: Rendir cuentas significa sencillamente que los creyentes velan con amor por el andar de los demás con Dios — animando, orando y corrigiendo con mansedumbre. Hace siglos, Juan Wesley reunía a los creyentes en pequeñas "clases" donde con regularidad se preguntaban unos a otros algo sencillo: ¿cómo está tu alma? Guardamos nuestras propias convicciones sobre los detalles, pero la idea es sana y bíblica: unos pocos creyentes de confianza que nos conozcan y nos hagan las preguntas honestas. Cuando alguno tropieza, el mandato es suave: "Hermanos, si alguno fuere tomado en alguna falta, vosotros que sois espirituales, restauradle con espíritu de mansedumbre... Sobrellevad los unos las cargas de los otros, y cumplid así la ley de Cristo" (Gálatas 6:1–2, RVG). La Palabra nos dice que seamos abiertos: "Confesaos vuestras faltas unos a otros, y orad los unos por los otros, para que seáis sanados" (Santiago 5:16, RVG). Y nos dice por qué nos necesitamos: "Hierro con hierro se aguza; y el hombre aguza el rostro de su amigo" (Proverbios 27:17, RVG). "Mejores son dos que uno... y cordón de tres dobleces no presto se rompe" (Eclesiastés 4:9, 12, RVG).

blocks.en: V. A Careful Caution and a Gentle Warning
blocks.es_reference: V. Una Advertencia Cuidadosa y una Precaución

blocks.en: We hold the priesthood of all believers: "But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood" (1 Peter 2:9, NKJV). Every believer has direct access to God through Christ, so we confess our sin first to God, and we may also confess to trusted brothers and sisters for prayer and healing — but never to a man as a required mediator. And accountability must always wear the face of love. It is voluntary, mutual, and tender. The moment it becomes harsh control, suspicion, or gossip, it has stopped being the gentle restoring of Galatians 6 and become something the Spirit never asked for. Guard one another; do not police one another.
blocks.es_reference: Sostenemos el sacerdocio de todos los creyentes: "Mas vosotros sois linaje escogido, real sacerdocio" (1 Pedro 2:9, RVG). Todo creyente tiene acceso directo a Dios por medio de Cristo; por eso confesamos nuestro pecado primero a Dios, y podemos también confesar a hermanos de confianza para oración y sanidad — pero nunca a un hombre como mediador obligatorio. Y la rendición de cuentas debe llevar siempre el rostro del amor. Es voluntaria, mutua y tierna. En el momento en que se vuelve control duro, sospecha o chisme, ha dejado de ser la restauración suave de Gálatas 6 para convertirse en algo que el Espíritu nunca pidió. Cuidaos los unos a los otros; no os vigiléis como policías.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: We cannot grow well alone, because God made us members of a body who need one another to grow. Find your place in a faithful church. Open your life to a few believers who will love you enough to tell you the truth. The foundation of all of it is not fear, nor duty, nor the wish to control, but the grace of God in Christ — the grace that saved us one by one and then bound us together in love.
blocks.es_reference: No podemos crecer bien a solas, porque Dios nos hizo miembros de un cuerpo que se necesitan los unos a los otros para crecer. Halle su lugar en una iglesia fiel. Abra su vida a unos pocos creyentes que lo amen lo suficiente como para decirle la verdad. El fundamento de todo ello no es el temor, ni el deber, ni el deseo de controlar, sino la gracia de Dios en Cristo — la gracia que nos salvó uno por uno y luego nos unió en amor.

mc.stem: What is the basic truth about the Christian life that this unit teaches?
options: The Christian life is a private matter between the believer and God alone
God saves us not only as individuals but into a body and a family, so we live the Christian life together
Community is optional for mature believers who can stand on their own
Fellowship is mainly for new converts until they grow strong

mc.stem: According to 1 Corinthians 12:27, what are believers in relation to Christ?
options: Servants hired to do His work
Students who graduate and move on
Guests who visit His house now and then
The body of Christ, and members individually

mc.stem: What does Romans 12:5 say about how believers relate to each other?
options: Though many, we are one body in Christ and individually members of one another
Only leaders are joined to the body
Each one stands completely independent of the rest
We are members of Christ but not of one another

mc.stem: What does Hebrews 10:25 warn against?
options: Meeting together too often
Listening to exhortation from others
Forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as some are in the habit of doing
Considering one another's needs

mc.stem: In Hebrews 10:24, why are we to consider one another?
options: To find reasons to leave the church
To compare ourselves and compete
To keep a record of others' faults
To stir up one another to love and good works

mc.stem: What is the 'new commandment' Jesus gives in John 13:34-35?
options: That we keep the law of Moses perfectly
That we love one another, so all will know we are His disciples
That we withdraw from the world entirely
That we judge one another strictly

mc.stem: What did the early church devote themselves to, according to Acts 2:42?
options: The apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers
Solitude and isolation
Politics and public debate
Building wealth and property

mc.stem: What does this unit mean by 'accountability' among believers?
options: A pastor ruling over members' private lives
Keeping a list of everyone's sins
Believers lovingly watching over one another's walk, encouraging and gently correcting
A government office that monitors the church

mc.stem: The unit traces the idea of small accountability groups partly to which historical practice?
options: The medieval monasteries' vows of silence
John Wesley's 'class meetings,' where believers asked one another how it was with their souls
The modern self-help movement
The Roman confessional booth

mc.stem: How should a believer overtaken in a fault be treated, according to Galatians 6:1?
options: Exposed publicly and shamed
Ignored until he recovers on his own
Removed from the church immediately
Restored gently, in a spirit of meekness, by those who are spiritual

mc.stem: What does Galatians 6:2 tell believers to do?
options: Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ
Avoid the troubles of others
Carry only their own load and let others carry theirs
Report one another's burdens to the authorities

mc.stem: What does James 5:16 instruct believers to do for one another?
options: Keep their sins entirely to themselves
Confess only to an ordained priest
Confess their trespasses to one another and pray for one another, that they may be healed
Announce their sins to the whole congregation

mc.stem: What is the meaning of 'iron sharpens iron' in Proverbs 27:17?
options: Conflict is always to be avoided at any cost
Believers should avoid friction with each other
Only strong personalities help the church
Close friends in Christ sharpen and strengthen one another

mc.stem: What does Ecclesiastes 4:9-12 teach?
options: One strong person is better than many weak ones
Two are better than one, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken
It is safest to walk through life alone
Friends are a distraction from God

mc.stem: How does the unit frame the 'priesthood of all believers' regarding confession?
options: Every believer has direct access to God, so we confess to God and may also confess to trusted believers, not to a priest as mediator
Confession to other believers is forbidden
Only the pastor may hear another's confession
Confession must always be made publicly to be valid

mc.stem: What is one danger the unit warns about in Christian community?
options: Loving one another too much
Praying for one another too often
Turning accountability into harsh control or gossip instead of gentle, loving care
Meeting together too frequently

mc.stem: According to the unit, accountability among believers is meant to be:
options: A substitute for a personal relationship with God
A one-way authority of leaders over members
A legal requirement enforced by penalties
Voluntary, mutual, and motivated by love, not forced or controlling

mc.stem: Why does the unit say Christians cannot grow well in isolation?
options: Because isolation makes us holier
Because God designed us as members of a body who need one another to grow
Because the Bible commands constant activity
Because solitude is sinful

mc.stem: How do the 'one anothers' of the New Testament shape community?
options: They apply only to church leaders
They are suggestions for special occasions
They call every believer to love, serve, encourage, forgive, and bear with one another
They replace the need for the local church

mc.stem: What is the proper foundation and motive for all Christian community and accountability?
options: The grace of God in Christ, which saves us and binds us together in love
A desire to control others
Earning God's acceptance by our effort
Fear of punishment

sa.prompt: Why does this unit say the Christian life is not meant to be lived alone? Use 1 Corinthians 12 or Romans 12.
sa.model: Paul says we are the body of Christ, and members individually (1 Corinthians 12:27), and that being many, we are one body in Christ and individually members of one another (Romans 12:5). The Christian life is not meant to be lived alone because each member is necessary to the rest — we do not attend the body of Christ, we are the body, and we grow together, not in isolation.

sa.prompt: What does Hebrews 10:24-25 teach about meeting together?
sa.model: Hebrews 10:24-25 teaches us to consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, but exhorting one another, and all the more as we see the Day approaching. Meeting together is not optional for the strong Christian; it is commanded, and it is the ordinary place where believers stir each other up to love and good works.

sa.prompt: What is the 'new commandment' of John 13:34-35, and what is its purpose?
sa.model: The 'new commandment' of John 13:34-35 is that we love one another, as Christ has loved us. Its purpose is that by this love, all people will know that we are His disciples — love for one another is the visible badge that identifies Christ's followers to the watching world.

sa.prompt: What does it mean to 'bear one another's burdens' in Galatians 6:2?
sa.model: To bear one another's burdens (Galatians 6:2) means to come alongside a fellow believer carrying a heavy load — sin, grief, weakness, or trial — and to help carry it with them rather than leaving them to struggle alone. Paul says doing this fulfills the law of Christ, which is love expressed in practical, shared help.

sa.prompt: How should we restore a believer who has fallen, according to Galatians 6:1?
sa.model: Galatians 6:1 says that if a believer is overtaken in any trespass, those who are spiritual should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, watching ourselves lest we also be tempted. Restoration is meant to be gentle and humble, not harsh or superior, remembering our own vulnerability to sin as we help another back up.

sa.prompt: What does James 5:16 say about confession and prayer among believers?
sa.model: James 5:16 says, 'Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed.' It teaches that honest confession among trusted believers, paired with prayer for one another, brings healing — sin confessed and prayed over in community does not stay hidden and does not remain unaddressed.

sa.prompt: Explain 'iron sharpens iron' (Proverbs 27:17) in Christian friendship.
sa.model: 'As iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the countenance of his friend' (Proverbs 27:17) pictures how close Christian friendship makes us better — through honest encouragement, correction, and accountability, a good friend strengthens our walk with God the way one piece of iron hones the edge of another, which cannot happen at a distance.

sa.prompt: What was John Wesley's 'class meeting,' and how can believers today use the idea?
sa.model: John Wesley gathered believers into small 'class meetings' where they regularly asked one another a simple question: how is it with your soul? Believers today can use the same idea by forming a few trusted relationships where honest questions about one's walk with God are welcomed and expected, rather than leaving spiritual life entirely private.

sa.prompt: How do we understand confession in light of the priesthood of all believers?
sa.model: We hold the priesthood of all believers (1 Peter 2:9): every believer has direct access to God through Christ, so we confess our sin first to God, not to a human mediator. We may also confess to trusted brothers and sisters for prayer and healing, but this is voluntary fellowship, never a required mediating step between us and God.

sa.prompt: What is the danger to avoid in accountability, and what is its right foundation?
sa.model: The danger to avoid in accountability is that it becomes harsh control, suspicion, or gossip rather than gentle restoration. Its right foundation is not fear, duty, or the wish to control, but the grace of God in Christ — accountability must always be voluntary, mutual, tender, and wear the face of love.
